subject: LLM usage boundary & evidence handoff for DPA — procurement sprint plan
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@wellcorehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@wellcorehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — LLM training exclusion and evidence needs

Hi Sean and team,

Thanks for walking us through the draft DPA last week. Procurement and Legal asked me to capture two things they need before we can progress: a short operational checklist showing how Redwood will ensure our interactions are excluded from model improvement (no-train), and a sample evidence pack we can hand to our auditors that shows data handling, retention, and subprocessor boundaries.

High-level asks: 
- A one-page operational checklist your ops team will follow on onboarding WellCore (prefix/KV handling, ephemeral session flags, SFTP export path, KMS residency).
- A sample evidentiary PDF demonstrating: subprocessor inventory, access logs (sample format), and proof of deletion for ephemeral sessions.
- Confirmation on ownership of prompts & generated responses (are outputs considered customer-owned artifacts or limited license to Redwood?).

Can you also confirm if there are any planned subprocessor transfers to third-party inference partners in the next 6 months? Legal will need advance notice if any transfer or cross-border processing is expected.

Target: procurement hopes to close the POC contract in the next two weeks; so if we can get these artifacts and a brief timeline, that would be very helpful.

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Senior Sourcing Manager, WellCore Health
attachments: none
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@wellcorehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — LLM training exclusion and evidence needs

Emily — thanks for the clear list. Quick ack and plan below.

Short plan (deliverables and owners):
1) Operational Checklist (1 page) — Sean (Ops liaison) + Marissa (Customer Onboarding) — delivery by 2026-11-30.
2) Evidence pack (sample PDF) — Kimberly (Legal) + Security — will provide a redacted pack showing subprocessor inventory + sample audit log snippets by 2026-12-01.
3) Prompt/output ownership statement — Kimberly to confirm legal language; pragmatic approach: customer retains ownership of inputs and outputs, Redwood provides a limited license for service operation (no rights to use outputs to train models for other customers).
4) Subprocessor transfers — no planned transfers for WellCore's designated region during the POC period; any change will be communicated 30 days in advance.

We're attaching a proposed evidence checklist and a draft DPA diff for your team to review (see attachments). If procurement wants an in-call walkthrough, we can schedule a 30-minute slot tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-evidence-checklist.pdf, proposed-dpa-diff.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@wellcorehealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — LLM training exclusion and evidence needs

Hi Emily, Sean —

Attached is a redacted sample evidence pack (PDF) and a short note on the proposed ownership clause. Executive summary first:

- Ownership: WellCore retains ownership of customer inputs and generated outputs. Redwood requests a service-limited license necessary to deliver inference (storage / caching for the duration of the session and short-term KV caching to meet latency SLOs). We explicitly exclude any rights to incorporate WellCore-originating data into model improvement pipelines or training datasets.Both the license and exclusion will be reflected in the DPA addendum.
- Subprocessors: Current processing uses Redwood-owned clusters and our managed storage providers. For the WellCore POC in the US region we do not plan to route requests to third-party inference partners. Any addition of a third-party inference subprocessor will require 
  a) 30 days notice
  b) explicit written approval for WellCore accounts that opt out of such subprocessors.
- Evidence pack: included items (redacted): subprocessor inventory, sample API access log (UTC timestamps), KMS key alias, sample deletion confirmation (showing record id and retention flag). 

Notes on proof of non-training: 
- We will tag POC traffic with a tenant-scoped no-train flag. That flag disables data ingestion into offline training pipelines and ensures ephemeral KV cache is not persisted into model training buckets.
- Audit artifact: daily digest showing "no-train" flag presence + storage lifecycle events for a 30-day window (we'll provide a sample csv).

Next steps: if this aligns with WellCore's requirements we'll update the DPA addendum text and produce a final evidence PDF for your auditors. If you want the operational checklist to include step-by-step SFTP export verification, tell us and Marissa will add it.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-evidence-checklist.pdf
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@wellcorehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@wellcorehealth.com, WellCore Legal <legal@wellcorehealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — LLM training exclusion and evidence needs

Thanks — this is exactly what procurement needs. A couple quick clarifications from Legal: 
- They want the DPA addendum clause to state "no use for model improvement, including but not limited to fine-tuning, re-training, or reinforcement of Redwood models" (explicit text preferred).
- They will review the sample audit csv; if the daily digest shows consistent "no-train" flags and deletion events, that's acceptable.

Procurement is ready to proceed with the POC contract conditioned on the final DPA addendum language and the evidence pack. Can we target sending the final DPA addendum by 2026-12-03 so procurement can route internally?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Emily
Emily Zhao
Senior Sourcing Manager, WellCore Health
